title: Impact of Magnetic Hysteresis on Inductance Profile Calculation and Model Predictive Control Performance in Switched Reluctance Motors
content: This paper investigates the influence of phase inductance identification accuracy on the modelling and control performance of switched reluctance motors (SRMs). Fundamental motor equations and representative operating waveforms are presented to highlight the importance of inductance profiles in electromagnetic torque prediction and control strategy development. Experimental investigations reveal that the identified phase inductance depends on the excitation frequency used during measurement. This phenomenon is examined using a parameter-fitted Jiles–Atherton hysteresis model incorporating the influence of the magnetic circuit air gap. The experimentally observed relationship is reproduced in the model and approximated using a power-law function, enabling the recalculation of inductance profiles to improve their consistency with torque-based measurements. The original and recalculated inductance profiles are subsequently evaluated using five control strategies, including three model predictive control (MPC) approaches. Control performance is assessed using three quality indices describing torque tracking accuracy, peak-to-peak torque ripple, and maximum torque deviation. The comparative results support the hypothesis that the proposed inductance recalculation substantially improves SRM control performance, demonstrating the importance of accurate magnetic characteristics in advanced control strategies.
